idea_summary: A marketplace where independent sellers list products, customers place orders, and administrators handle refunds.

functional_requirements.statement: Independent sellers can list products with details such as name, price, and description.
acceptance_criteria: Product details must be submitted and stored in the database successfully.

functional_requirements.statement: Customers can browse products and place orders.
acceptance_criteria: Customer must be able to search, browse, and add products to their cart.

functional_requirements.statement: Customers can view and manage their order statuses.
acceptance_criteria: Order status updates must be visible to the customer in real-time.

functional_requirements.statement: Administrators can handle refunds and issue refunds once the request is approved.
acceptance_criteria: Refund must be issued when the administrator approves the request.

non_functional_requirements.statement: Payment system must ensure idempotency to prevent multiple charges for a single payment.
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: Automated tests checking payment system's response to multiple requests.

non_functional_requirements.statement: System must maintain inventory consistency across all operations.
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: Regular inventory audits and API checks.

non_functional_requirements.statement: Refund process must have an audit trail for compliance.
non_functional_requirements.target: Data must be stored for at least 5 years.

non_functional_requirements.statement: System must handle failed payments gracefully.
non_functional_requirements.target: 24-hour response time for failed payment notifications.
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: Monitoring alerts and support ticket responses.

obligation_coverage.design_response: The system design includes role-based access control (RBAC) where only authorized sellers can add products. Each product is linked to its owner seller ID.
The Payment Gateway component ensures idempotency by storing transaction IDs to prevent duplicate transactions.
The Refund Audit Component logs all refund requests and issues, maintaining an immutable audit trail.
The backend service updates inventory in a single, transactional operation to ensure consistency across all operations.
Integration tests simulate failed payment scenarios to ensure the system can handle errors gracefully.

assumptions.statement: All transactions will be processed through a secure payment gateway.
